answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and claims one ridge walnut tree felled by a gale, paying 34 credits first and 6 more per later claim, so the thousandth pays 6028. It clears the tree and files a key-signed log with its stump serial and gale damage record. A ridge auditor checks the register for serial and key match; reuse or mismatch burns the bond and cancels the identity. A rented-clearance ring fails: the stump serial is already claimed under another key. One thousand fakes pay 3,031,000 in fees and lock 70,000; an honest identity pays 34 once and recovers its bond.
